霧.meaning: A lazy cloud is handed one <part>task</part> on a clipboard: '<part>rain</part> on the cabbage farm.' Too sleepy to fall, it lies down across the field and breathes its drops out as a grey hush. The farmer walks straight into his own scarecrow. The job got done, sort of: as <kanji>fog</kanji>.
霧.on: Out of the grey, a <sound>moo</sound>se wanders past with a cabbage stuck on each antler.
霧.kun: The farmer gropes along the wall for his door <sound>key</sound> and grabs a wet <sound>ree</sound>d instead.

渇.meaning: A snail crawls under a beach <part>sunshade</part>, dragging herself toward three <part>water drops</part> on the hot sand. Each time she nearly reaches one, it sizzles away. By the third, her eye stalks are drooping like wilted flowers. Even a snail can feel <kanji>thirst</kanji>.
渇.on: The beach café offers her a crispy <sound>katsu</sound> cutlet, which only makes her mouth drier.
渇.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in a rock pool spits a drop her way, and she cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!' with joy.

廊.meaning: A farmer's <part>son</part> wants a bigger room, so he keeps adding planks to the garden <part>shed</part>, one door at a time. Soon it runs the whole length of the farm, long and narrow, with doors on both sides. His mum needs a bike to bring him tea down the <kanji>corridor</kanji>.
廊.on: At the far end, by the last door, he grows a single red <sound>ro</sound>se in a pot.

祉.meaning: Beside a bus <part>stop</part> stands an old <part>lamppost</part> that has decided to look after the town. It glows warm for anyone waiting late, hangs a scarf on its arm for the cold and keeps a bowl of milk at its foot for strays. The council gives it a medal for public <kanji>welfare</kanji>.
祉.on: The medal is painted on a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld and bolted to the post, just under the light.

痴.meaning: A man who says he can <part>know</part> anything from books lives in a <part>leaky shed</part>. When it rains, he puts a bucket on his head instead of fixing the roof and reads a book about roofs from underneath it. His goat fixes the roof. Knowing all that and doing nothing is plain <kanji>stupid</kanji>.
痴.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah strolls in out of the rain and smirks at him from the one dry corner.
痴.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p pokes its head through the hole in the roof and drips all over his book.

暦.meaning: A hermit plants a <part>grove</part> in a long line under a <part>cliff</part>. Each morning the <part>sun</part> peeks over the edge, and the cliff's shadow points at a different tree. He names every tree after a day. When the shadow reaches the last one, he throws a New Year party. His grove is a <kanji>calendar</kanji>.
暦.on: From a <sound>wre</sound>ck on the beach below he salvages a rusty <sound>key</sound> and hangs it on the first tree.
暦.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala in the first tree eats one pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt a day, and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat counts the empty pots.

娘.meaning: An old <part>woman</part> knits a rag doll, and it comes out so <part>good</part> that it sits up, rubs its button eyes and calls her 'Mum'. She tucks it into bed, buys it tiny shoes and teaches it to whistle. Now she has a <kanji>daughter</kanji>.
娘.on: The doll's best friend is a <sound>jo</sound>ey that hops out of the sock basket every morning.
娘.kun: A cow at the window says '<sound>Mu</sound>!', and the girl feeds it <sound>su</sound>shi and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

孫.meaning: Granny ties one end of her knitting to her rocking chair and the other to a cradle in the next town. The yarn of the <part>lineage</part> runs past her son's house on the way. At the far end sleeps a brand new <part>child</part>, holding the thread tight: her first <kanji>grandchild</kanji>.
孫.on: Granny comes to visit in a huge <sound>som</sound>brero, which she holds over the cradle for shade.
孫.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' gurgles the baby, and a <sound>go</sound>pher pops out of the lawn to see.

卸.meaning: At <part>noon</part> a farmer drives up with a truck of ten thousand eggs. The shopkeeper counts them, nods '<part>correct</part>', and bangs one huge rubber <part>stamp</part> on the whole truck instead of pricing each egg. Nobody here buys just one: it's all <kanji>wholesale</kanji>.
卸.on: The next truck brings crate after crate of <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock feathers, and the stamp lands on all of it at once.
卸.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' squeaks a <sound>ro</sound>dent, as the last truck unloads a whole mountain of cheese for the shops.

墨.meaning: A mole digs so deep that the <part>soil</part> turns <part>black</part> and sticky. She dips her claw in it and signs her name on a stone. An old monk sees it, rolls the dirt into sticks and grinds one with water for his brush. The mole has found <kanji>black ink</kanji>.
墨.on: The monk's <sound>box</sound>er dog licks the brush and walks around with a black tongue.
墨.kun: His cook, <sound>Sue</sound>, spills the pot on a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, which scampers off with brand new stripes.

征.meaning: A strict teacher rides the <part>chairlift</part> up to a mountain town where every shop sign is spelled wrong. She marks each one in red until it's <part>correct</part>, and the rebels hand over their crayons one by one. Without a single sword, she manages to <kanji>subjugate</kanji> the whole town.
征.on: She locks their crayons in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe and keeps the only key.

賊.meaning: At midnight a crab tiptoes into a pearl shop holding a tiny <part>spear</part>. It pries open <part>ten</part> <part>shellfish</part> one by one, pockets every pearl and leaves a note: 'Sorry, I needed a necklace.' By morning the whole harbour is hunting a very small <kanji>burglar</kanji>.
賊.on: 'It went that way!' says <sound>Zo</sound>e, the night guard, while her <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock squawks along.

笛.meaning: A panda bites holes in a hollow stick of <part>bamboo</part> to get at a beetle hiding inside. When she breathes on it, it sings. She spends all spring looking for the <part>reason</part>, then gives up and plays tunes for the other pandas. She has made a <kanji>flute</kanji>.
笛.on: Her fans send her a <sound>te</sound>xt message after every tune: 'More!'
笛.kun: She plays a lullaby from her <sound>fu</sound>ton until an <sound>e</sound>gg in the nest above hatches.

汽.meaning: A dragon has a cold and can't breathe fire. Every time it tries, it just sprays <part>water drops</part> that hiss on its hot teeth and drift off as <part>steam</part>. The village laughs, then lines up to iron their shirts in front of it. Their dragon now breathes nothing but <kanji>vapor</kanji>.
汽.on: To start it each morning, the villagers turn a big brass <sound>key</sound> in its ear.

慌.meaning: A tidy gardener comes home from holiday to find her lawn gone <part>wild</part>: hedges like monsters, a goat on the roof. Her <part>heartbeat</part> leaps. She runs about with the watering can upside down and puts her hat on the cat. She is completely <kanji>disconcerted</kanji>.
慌.on: The goat calmly licks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne it found in the shed.
慌.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she shrieks, and then '<sound>Wah</sound>!' as she drops the can on her own foot.

剰.meaning: A delivery girl takes a long <part>ride</part> across town with one giant pizza for twelve guests. At the party she cuts it into twelve with her little <part>dagger</part>, and only two guests turn up. Ten slices are left over, so she rides home with a <kanji>surplus</kanji>.
剰.on: On the way she gives one slice to a <sound>jo</sound>ey hopping beside the road.
剰.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>Ma</sound>!' squeals the joey; she sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and hands it a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and an <sound>e</sound>gg besides.

韓.meaning: A traveller buys a sizzling <part>kebab</part> at a night market and climbs a tall <part>pagoda</part> to eat it with a view. The wind steals her napkin and drapes it over the bell on top, which rings out across the snowy hills. She waves sorry to the monks below and writes a postcard: 'Loving <kanji>Korea</kanji>.'
韓.on: A monk climbs up anyway and tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation behind her ear to say welcome.
韓.kun: In the temple pond a <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps for her last crumb, and the monks cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

赦.meaning: A judge turns <part>red</part> with rage at a boy who stole her lunch. Sweat pours down her face. The boy opens a paper <part>fan</part> and fans her until she cools down and starts to giggle. She bangs her hammer and grants him a <kanji>pardon</kanji>.
赦.on: His only punishment: fetch every <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock stuck on the courthouse roof.
赦.kun: To say thank you, he leaves a <sound>eu</sound>calyptus leaf on her bench, and a <sound>roo</sound>k flies off with it.

頻.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> decides to <part>walk</part> all the way round the rim of the bath. Plop, it falls in. It climbs out and tries again. Plop. Every night, the same lap and the same splash. It falls in <kanji>repeatedly</kanji> and never gives up.
頻.on: The bathroom door's <sound>hin</sound>ge squeaks every time someone peeks in to check on it.
頻.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p and a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird keep score in soap on the shower curtain.

沖.meaning: A fisherman tired of crowded beaches rows until the land is gone and there are only <part>water drops</part> on every side. He plants a tiny flag on a float: 'the <part>middle</part>'. A whale surfaces beside it, puzzled. He has made it to the <kanji>open sea</kanji>.
沖.on: He sits by his flag and blows bubbles of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum at the whale.
沖.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a passing gull, and drops a <sound>ki</sound>wi fruit into his boat.

仁.meaning: A café has one <part>coat hook</part> by the door with <part>two</part> warm coats on it: one for the owner and one for whoever needs it. A shivering stranger takes the spare and leaves a thank-you note in the pocket. That spare coat is the café's <kanji>humanity</kanji>.
仁.on: Each pocket also holds a warm <sound>gin</sound>ger biscuit for the road.

循.meaning: A ski resort hangs a numbered <part>shield</part> from each seat of its <part>chairlift</part>. The skiers must hop off in order, one, two, three, with no skipping ahead. A rabbit tries to jump the queue and is sent straight to the back. Everything here is <kanji>sequential</kanji>.
循.on: Each seat brushes past the same <sound>jun</sound>iper bush in turn, and every skier sniffs it.

褒.meaning: A grandma sews a fluffy <part>garment</part> around her shivering hedgehog to <part>protect</part> it from frost. The hedgehog parades round the village in it, and everyone stops to clap and shout 'Well stitched!' Grandma blushes at all the <kanji>praise</kanji>.
褒.on: The gardener next door cheers by spraying a rainbow from her <sound>ho</sound>se.
褒.kun: Guests lean out of every <sound>ho</sound>tel window to cheer the little hedgehog on.

媒.meaning: At a dance, a <part>woman</part> pushes two shy strangers together: 'Meet <part>so-and-so</part>, this is so-and-so!' She can't remember either name, but they start talking anyway and marry the next spring. She was their <kanji>mediator</kanji>.
媒.on: She rides a tandem <sound>bi</sound>ke behind them all the way to the wedding.
媒.kun: At the party she hands round <sound>na</sound>an, an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne each and a toy <sound>do</sound>lphin for the bride.

凡.meaning: A famous artist unveils her new work: a plain kitchen <part>table</part> with one <part>dot</part> of paint on it. The crowd waits for something more. Nothing happens. A man sets his teacup down on it. Even the critics agree: it's <kanji>commonplace</kanji>.
凡.on: Someone puts a tiny <sound>bon</sound>sai next to the dot, and the crowd yawns even harder.
凡.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' shrugs the man, spooning <sound>yo</sound>gurt off the table, 'it's about what I expected.'

把.meaning: In a storm, a sailor's <part>bed</part> slides across the cabin. Without waking, he reaches out one hand, grabs the <part>anchor</part> chain beside it and holds on all night, snoring. In the morning the chain is still locked in his fist's <kanji>grasp</kanji>.
把.on: Back on shore, he sleeps in a little <sound>hu</sound>t and still grips the bedpost every night.

圏.meaning: A wizard keeps his spell book, a thick <part>volume</part>, locked in a round <part>cage</part>. When he opens the door, a glowing bubble swells out and rolls over the whole village: inside it, every cat can talk. Nobody wants to step outside the magic's <kanji>sphere</kanji>.
圏.on: His dog stays in its <sound>ken</sound>nel just past the bubble's edge, barking like any dog.
圏.kun: He rings a <sound>ca</sound>rp pond and a <sound>ko</sound>ala's tree with a circle of stones: an enclosure.

督.meaning: Every Saturday your <part>uncle</part> stands at the edge of the pool with a whistle, keeping one hawk <part>eye</part> on the children. 'Elbows up! Kick!' Nobody dares slow down. He can barely swim himself, but he's a great <kanji>coach</kanji>.
督.on: Even the pool clock obeys him: tick-<sound>tock</sound>, right in time with his whistle.

偵.meaning: In a hotel lobby, a long trench coat hangs from a <part>coat hook</part>, standing a little too <part>upright</part>. Its collar turns to follow each guest, and two eyes blink behind the buttonholes. Someone has hidden inside to listen: a <kanji>spy</kanji>.
偵.on: He sticks secret notes under the tables with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.

澄.meaning: A muddy pond is ashamed of its brown water. One hot day its <part>water drops</part> <part>ascend</part> into the sky as mist, leaving the mud behind, and fall back at night as rain. By morning a fish can see the stars from the bottom. The pond shines with <kanji>lucidity</kanji>.
澄.on: A frog finds a lost pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker on the bottom, sparkling in the clear water.
澄.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef drops in a single grain of rice and can still see it on the bottom.
